title: Walker Morris builds on AI investment with Legora partnership
summary: Walker Morris has partnered with Legora, the agentic operating system for legal work, building on its existing use of AI tools and its continued investment in the skills, technology and training shaping the delivery of its legal services.
body_markdown:
Walker Morris has partnered with Legora, the agentic operating system for legal work, building on its existing use of AI tools and its continued investment in the skills, technology and training shaping the delivery of its legal services. The partnership follows a successful pilot tailored to individual practice areas, with leads developing workflows focused on client needs.


Innovation is a core pillar of Walker Morris’ Ambition 27 strategy, supporting sustainable growth and the delivery of complex, high-value legal work. This latest investment in Legora forms part of the firm’s continued investment in its people and technology.


The rollout will give all of the firm's 300+ lawyers access to Legora, alongside other firmwide AI tools, including Microsoft Copilot and Lexis+ AI Protégé. The firm has introduced a structured, mandatory training and education programme for all fee earners focused on safe, responsible and effective use, maintaining the quality of legal advice and identifying where AI can deliver the greatest value for clients.


Walker Morris has taken a hands-on approach to adoption, working with partners and practice area leaders to identify how AI can support client relationships. This includes helping clients pursue their own AI ambitions and equipping junior lawyers with AI and innovation skills to deliver meaningful client value from the outset of their careers. The firm is also using super user groups involving colleagues at all levels to design workflows and standardised prompts for all fee earners.


**Jeanette Burgess, Managing Partner at Walker Morris,** said: "Our investment in Legora builds on the work already underway across the firm to use AI responsibly and effectively. A key part of this is equipping our lawyers with the skills and judgement to ensure continued delivery of high-quality advice as legal services evolve. Our priority is enhancing the client experience and giving our lawyers more time to devote to the issues that matter most to clients; providing clear and practical solutions to complex legal issues, applying commercial judgement and investing in relationships."


**Laura Pilkington, Innovation Lead at Walker Morris,** added: "We are building on our work to embed AI and innovation into everyday legal practice, at every level of seniority. For trainees and junior lawyers, that means hands-on experience alongside the development of strong legal foundations, including opportunities to share knowledge and contribute to clients’ innovation goals. For senior lawyers, it means developing the AI literacy and practical experience to supervise its use effectively, support the next generation and improve their own ways of working."


**Alex Fortescue-Webb, Head of UK & Ireland at Legora,** said: "Walker Morris's lawyers learned to develop their workflows alongside our legal engineers, and are now training colleagues in their own practice groups. When firms have a strong group of champions like this, usage across the rest of the firm more than doubles, because lawyers pick up AI faster from a colleague who has already used it on real work."
